{{Recipe}}

This layered Malaysian '''kuih lapis''' is made using wheat flour and cornstarch. It has a chewy texture.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]] 
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Cornstarch|cornstarch]] 
* ½ cup granulated [[Cookbook:White Sugar|white sugar]] 
* 4 cups medium-thick [[Cookbook:Coconut Milk|coconut milk]] 
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] 
* [[Cookbook:Food Coloring|Food coloring]] as desired

==Procedure==
# Preheat a [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]] in a [[Cookbook:Steamer|steamer]] over a pot of simmering water. 
# Combine the flour, cornstarch, sugar, coconut milk, and salt in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]]. Process until completely smooth, then [[Cookbook:Straining|strain]] the batter. 
# Divide the batter into two bowls. Use food coloring to color each bowl a different color as desired.
# Pour a thin layer of one batter into the baking pan in the steamer, making sure it's evenly distributed. Cover and let [[Cookbook:Steaming|steam]] for 3 minutes. 
# Uncover the steamer, and pour an equally thin layer of the other batter on top of the first layer. Cover and let steam for 3 minutes.
# Repeat the layering and steaming process, alternating colors, until you have used up all your batter.
# Remove the pan from the steamer, and allow it to cool completely.
# Unmold the kuih from the pan, and cut it into pieces.
